criteria.criterion: defaults.toml gains a [[default]] with id "pinned-versions" whose statement is ONE sentence (no '. ' inside) saying config version pins such as claude_version stay exact and never float, are bumped only by `cargo run -p xtask -- repin`, and a refusal from a mismatch names that command, marked prose-only. Check with Grep on defaults.toml.
criteria.evidence: I read defaults.toml lines 105-109 (diff and Grep). The statement "Config version pins such as claude_version stay exact and never float, they are bumped only by `cargo run -p xtask -- repin`, a refusal from a mismatch names that command, and the rule is prose-only with no enforcement code yet." contains no '. ' before its final period. render() cuts at the first '. ' (defaults.rs:77-83), so the whole rule renders.

summary: The change passes. It adds two prose-only defaults, pinned-versions and explicit-tool-paths, to the end of defaults.toml. Each rule is a single sentence with no '. ' inside it, which matters because the reader shows only the first sentence of each default; the new test confirms the whole rule appears. No existing default was edited. A second new test checks that all 16 earlier rendered lines are unchanged. The reader budget goes from 2000 to 2200 tokens. The reader set now measures 2189 tokens, so 2200 is the smallest multiple of 50 that fits, and no other budget changed. The docs and the hard-coded figure in run_pin_tests.rs were updated to match, and no stale figures remain. On this snapshot I ran the budgets tests (9 of 9 passed) and the run_pin reader test (passed). For fmt, clippy and the full test suite I relied on Athena's recorded CI results, which all passed. Only the 7 expected files changed. The one finding is a nit: the changelog entry is long and dense.
